item: The launcher row readers decode a byte-order mark and report lines they could not read (R175 A)
summary: Before: a launcher record file saved with a UTF-8 byte-order mark lost its first row without a word (2 of 3 rows found), and one saved as UTF-16 lost every row and read as 'the launcher left nothing' (0 of 3), in all three files (measured 17 Oct on real files). Now the three readers decode with utf-8-sig, count the non-blank lines that are not a row, and add unparsed_lines to the block only when it is above 0 (absent = 0, so a clean file's block is the same bytes); a file that holds lines and no row is returned as unreadable with how many lines it held (launcher_exit/launcher_stop: kind unreadable, unreadable_files; launcher_stderr: unreadable true, lines_recorded null), and the report says unreadable, never 'no record'. The count is of lines after a UTF-8 decode, so for a UTF-16 file it counts fragments. Windows PowerShell 5.1 and a real console not run; PowerShell's own trim turned BOM and UTF-16 files into clean UTF-8 on pwsh 7 (Linux). Tests: 18 new (14 red without), two existing tests changed to the new answer for a file of only junk.
